Left Rotate Array by k number (optimal) class Solution { public void leftRotate(int[] nums, int k) { int n = nums.length; k = k % n; reverse(nums, 0, k - 1); reverse(nums, k, n - 1); reverse(nums, 0, n - 1); } public void reverse(int[] nums, int start, int end) { while (start < end) { int temp = nums[start]; nums[start] = nums[end]; nums[end] = temp; start++; end--; } } }

General NSS Interview Questions: Why do you want to join NSS? “I want to actively contribute to social causes and help make a difference. NSS gives me a chance to serve the community and grow as a person.” What does NSS mean to you? “To me, NSS is about selfless service, leadership, and making a positive impact on society.” Have you done any volunteering or community service before? (Talk about school events, donation drives, clean-up programs, etc. Even small contributions count.) What qualities make you a good fit for NSS? “I’m responsible, work well in teams, and genuinely care about helping others.” 🔹 Marketing-Specific Interview Questions: Why did you choose the marketing portfolio? “I enjoy creative work and communication. I want to help NSS reach more students and spread awareness about our activities.” What do you understand by marketing in the context of NSS? “Marketing in NSS is about promoting events, sharing our impact, and encouraging more participation through posters, social media, and word of mouth.” Do you have any experience with marketing or content creation? (You can talk about handling social media, making posters, organizing school events, etc.) How would you promote an NSS event on campus? Example answer: “I’d create attractive posters, reels, and stories for social media, share in student groups, and also spread the word in person with creative hooks.” Can you work under pressure with deadlines? “Yes. I understand that events can be fast-paced, and I’m good at staying calm and meeting deadlines.” Which social media platforms do you think are best for NSS promotions? Why? “Instagram is great for visual content and reels, while WhatsApp helps in quick updates. Both are effective for student engagement.” 🔹 Behavioral Questions: Tell us about a time you worked in a team. (Use a school/college project or event example. Focus on teamwork and communication.) What would you do if your team members don’t agree with your idea? “I’d try to understand their perspective and explain mine respectfully.
